rationale.usefulness: Operator rule: agents become stickier the longer they stay on a project (hazard aging), so redirect early; hopping is one-way drift to new work, not rotation. Moderate value: a negative on cycles plus a positive on dwell aging.

one_line: Project hops carry no circulation beyond age drift (cycle affinity above a calibrated age walker in 0/9 shared-goal unit-channels); net flow to newer projects is small (30/37 positive) and dwell hazards age (32/39), not geometric.

models.note: no cycle-driven broken detailed balance in project hops; irreversibility is age drift only
sticky Potts walker with habit and age bias fits triples; its geometric dwell fails (hazards age)
project hopping is excess (net occupancy change toward new projects), not housekeeping

v2.claim: Project hopping carries no circulation beyond the drift from older to newer projects (rotation-summed cycle affinity beyond a calibrated age walker in 0/9 unit-channels; power 0.55–0.97 for a 2-nat cycle), and the hazard of leaving a project falls with time already spent on it (32/39 unit-channels)
v2.scope: 9 testable shared-goal unit-channels; natives G38, G44, #51

ladder.factor: synthetic validation with two nulls (age walker, time reversal)

v2.decision: project switching is age drift plus trap aging, not a cycle; long-dwelling agents are the hardest to move
